messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: EDR
parts:
> > Are effective detection radii affected by left-truncation? In my case,
> > I truncated all detections within 12.5 m - based on examinations of
> > distance vs. frequency histograms.

They are not in the sense that, if you had perfect data, left-truncation
would still give the same estimate of effective detection radius on
average. However, you need to be very clear on what is causing a problem
with your data, before deciding whether left-truncation is appropriate.

Left-truncation is more commonly used for line transect sampling, e.g. in
aerial surveys where it becomes apparent that some animals close to the
line are being missed. In point-transect sampling, you might for example
get songbirds in dense cover that stop singing when you are very near,
causing you to miss them. Or birds near the point may flee undetected,
beyond the range of detection, leaving a 'hole' around the point.
Left-truncation might help in either case. However, if birds move a
little away from the point, so that you get too few detections near the
point but too many at middle distances, left-truncation will cause you to
overestimate density; better then not to truncate, so that the excess at
mid-distances tends to average out with the shortage near the point.
Similar considerations apply if birds are attracted towards the point -
though in this case, you must be careful not to use a model for the
detection function that fits the artificial 'spike' at zero.

Steve Buckland
